subject: Ingest windowing offsets and tenant-split on April invoice
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme-analytics.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Question: ingest windowing & tenant split on April invoice

Hi Priyom —

We just received the April invoice and noticed a ~38% jump on the ‘ingest’ line compared to March. Our engineering team pointed us at what looks like a windowing/tenant-split issue: a number of bulk uploads that started before the midnight UTC cutover appear to have been attributed to both staging and prod tenants for the same customer.

Key details:
- Invoice: April 2027 (attached snapshot)
- Example session ids: sess_7f9a, sess_7f9b, sess_81c0
- We are EU-headquartered — VAT calculations matter for our finance team

Can you confirm whether Redwood’s attribution window could have double-counted events for multi-tenant uploads? I attached a small CSV from our side with timestamps. We’d like to resolve before our accounts payable closes on Apr 10.

Attachments: ingest_log_sample.csv (CSV, 180KB), april_invoice_snapshot.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

Thanks —
Elena Morales
Head of Finance, Acme Analytics
elena.morales@acme-analytics.com
+44 20 7946 0XXX
From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: ingest windowing & tenant split on April invoice

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the detailed note and the attachments — that’s helpful. We’re pulling the billing and ingestion traces for the tenant IDs you referenced. A couple quick asks while we investigate:

1) Can you confirm whether those bulk uploads used the same API key across staging/prod or were separate keys per environment? That will change attribution behavior.
2) If you have any sample payload_ids or request_ids from your logs, include them — they speed up the join against our ingest ledger.

Initial theory: if uploads cross our daily boundary and you have both an org-level tenant and a project-level tenant configured, our current attribution logic can, in rare edge cases, attach overlapping sessions to both tenants for the same raw events during processing backfills. We have a repro in a test cluster but need to validate against your real ids.

We’ll run a targeted reconciliation and come back with line-by-line counts and a proposed credit if we find double-counts. I’ll loop in Ben to check whether this also affects tokenization (which would impact VATable units).

I’ll follow up by EOD with an ETA for the recon.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 13:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: ingest windowing & tenant split on April invoice

Elena / team —

Quick technical note from my side after a first pass on the exported ingest ledger for the tenant range Elena provided:

- I see a cluster of request_ids that span 2027-03-31T23:55:XXZ → 2027-04-01T00:05:XXZ (UTC). For ledger grouping we currently use a combination of request_id + occurrence_timestamp + tenant_id. If the same request was replayed during backfill under a different tenant_id, it would appear as two separate billed entries.
- Tokenization step: some of these large bulk uploads contain composite documents that are tokenized per-file. If both staging and prod keys point to the same org storage and a reingest job ran, token counts can double.

I attached a tiny recon CSV with the request_id window and a suggested dedupe heuristic (match on original_payload_checksum). If you can run a checksum on your side for the sample rows and share the checksum values, we can definitively dedupe.

Attachment: recon_small_batch.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Proposed next steps:
1) Customer to confirm API key usage + payload checksum for sample rows
2) Redwood to run dedupe and provide adjusted token tally + provisional credit quote
3) If confirmed, Accounting (Marissa) to issue a credit memo in April close (we can backdate to the invoice date)

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme-analytics.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:46:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Question: ingest windowing & tenant split on April invoice

Thanks Ben —

We confirmed with engineering: the bulk loader used a shared org key during the window because of a deploy mistake; that explains the duplicate tenant attribution. I’ve pulled the checksums for the three sample request_ids and pasted them below:

- sess_7f9a / req_1182: checksum a3f9b4c2
- sess_7f9b / req_1183: checksum a3f9b4c2
- sess_81c0 / req_1199: checksum d4b2e798

I attached the raw timestamps and request_ids for a 30-minute window around the boundary. Please let me know the expected credit and whether that will affect our VAT calculation for the month (we need to report correct VAT on our liability report).

Attachments: ingest_log_sample.csv (replaced with expanded 300KB), april_invoice_snapshot.pdf

— Elena
From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: Proposed credit and accounting action for ACME invoice 2027-04

Marissa / Ben —

Summary of findings:
- Root cause: shared org API key during midnight UTC boundary caused reingest under multiple tenant_ids; payload checksum confirms duplicate entries for a subset of requests (see Elena’s checksums).
- Impact: ~4,320 tokens double-counted across the three example sessions; extrapolated impact across the affected date range (23:50–00:10 UTC) yields ~18,700 tokens (0.0187k tokens) billed twice.

Recommendation:
1) Issue a provisional credit of €12.45 (computed using their per-token price tier and VAT-exempt net where applicable). We should mark the credit memo with note: 'Duplicate ingest attribution — provisional credit pending final recon'.
2) For VAT: because both duplicates are within the same billing entity and no cross-border supply changed, VAT liability remains unchanged — treat credit as adjustment to net taxable amount; confirm with legal if they require a separate VAT credit document.
3) Follow-up: schedule a short post-mortem with ACME engineering to discuss guardrails (org-key scoping, automated boundary checks).

I’ll open HubSpot ticket HS-1234567 and upload the evidence folder. Please proceed with a draft credit memo and let me know if you need any further breakdown for auditing.

— Priyom
Senior Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
